subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: When an explicitly configured `gateway.bind=tailnet` cannot resolve a bindable Tailscale IPv4 address, should the gateway remain available on loopback with a visible degraded-state warning, or fail startup?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: loopback preserves local availability and reduces network exposure, while fatal startup more strictly enforces the operator's requested reachability. Current documentation promises the fallback, so automation should not change this contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Warn and degrade to loopback
options.body: Keep the existing safe fallback, add a prominent startup warning and status/diagnostic indication, and cover the degraded path with focused tests.

options.title: Fail explicit Tailnet startup
options.body: Reject startup when an explicit Tailnet bind is unavailable, with compatibility notes and proof covering upgrades, transient Tailscale failures, and service restart behavior.

options.title: Add an explicit strict policy
options.body: Preserve the current default while adding an opt-in fail-closed policy, accepting the cost of another configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Warn and degrade to loopback
recommendation.body: Keep the existing safe fallback, add a prominent startup warning and status/diagnostic indication, and cover the degraded path with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Tailscale guidance work and live issue linkage make this the strongest available routing candidate for the compatibility-versus-availability decision.
